title: docs(agents): a "verified" claim points at the instrument, never at its answer
body:
Fixes #7833

Director seat ruling, summon #20, decision batch #108 item 5, route **A**: objectui's `AGENTS.md` gains one rule — a claim that something was verified is only as good as the check that re-verifies it on every commit — stated in the shape the repo has converged on three times: when declaring something verified, point at the instrument (the script or test that re-derives it), never write the number or the assertion itself.

⚠️ **The maintainer finalises the wording.** This PR lands a draft of it. See the 「维护者速读」 comment below for the options in letter form.

## What landed

One bullet, `#9`, at the end of section 5 「Coding Standards (the Commandments)」, plus a changeset. That is the whole diff.

> **#9 — A "verified" claim is only as good as the check that re-verifies it (objectui#7833).** Prose that declares something checked, counted, aligned or covered — in a doc, a code comment, a script or workflow header, or this file — states a fact that was derived once, when it was written, and is derived never again; no later reading can tell such an assertion from a live one. So when you declare something verified, **point at the instrument that re-derives it — the script, the gate, the test — and never write down its answer**: "the count this gate prints", not the count; "the list this script enumerates", not the list. A figure that is still correct is the dangerous case, not the safe one — a reader who spot-checks it confirms it and is still wrong once the population it described has moved out from under it. Where nothing re-derives the claim, say that in the text rather than let it read as live. This file is not exempt: it has carried such a claim and needed a repair (objectui#7800). The measured instances behind this rule sit on objectui#7833 — pointed at, not copied here, which is this rule applied to itself.

## ⭐ The rule carries no figure of its own — deliberately

A rule that says "never write the number" and then writes one is an instance of the defect it names, landing in the most-read file in the repo. So the text names **no** count of anything. The evidence is reached the way the rule prescribes: by **address**, not by copy — `objectui#7833` carries the measured instances, and a card number is an address, not a measurement. Reproducing the list here in the file would have restarted exactly the clock the rule is about.

Checked against the narrow pattern the objectui#7448 twins pin (a numeral qualifying a document-population noun): the bullet contains no numeral at all outside the issue references, which that pattern excludes by construction.

## Why section 5, in English, and not section 9

Placement decided the language, not the other way round.

- The artefacts the rule governs — docs, code comments, script and workflow headers — are **precisely** the ones commandment `#-1` enumerates when it says the codebase is English-only: *"code comments, docs (`README.md`, `docs/*.md`)"*. The parenthetical that grants Chinese is scoped to *"operational sections"* of this instruction file; section 5 is not one of them.
- Section 5 is the repo's list of **standards for what you write**, and it already carries a documentation commandment (`#2`) and a principle-plus-shape commandment (`#0.1`, contract-first). This rule is the same species: a principle and a fixed shape, no mechanism, no process, no checklist.
- Section 9 is operational discipline for driving the tooling in this repo. It is the *richest* neighbourhood for the idea — it already holds 「没跑对照的空结果不是一次读数」 and 「每次发布后回读」, which are the read-time half of the same principle — but the rule being landed here is the **write-time** half, and it must reach contributors who never open those subsections.

The alternative placement is a real one and the maintainer can take it; it is option **B** in the 速读 below.

## The evidence — measured, not asserted

The five instances the card measured this round:

| instance | the claim | how it went false |
|:--|:--|:--|
| objectui#7505 | a doc fragment marked "checked against the shipped `dist/index.d.ts`" | the gate **structurally cannot** compile a `declared` fragment, so nothing ever re-checked it — false **twice** |
| objectui#7528 | "one total over 52 chunks" in present-tense prose | three counts in play at once: the prose, the file's own frozen baseline, and the gate's live output |
| objectui#7362 | a fix list enumerated by name | entries expired as they were fixed; nothing re-derived the list |
| objectui#7433 | a population count | rotted three times |
| objectui#7448 | `184 pages (144 .mdx + 40 .md)` | a **precisely correct** count of the population the gate had **stopped having** — a reader who spot-checked it would have confirmed it and still been wrong about the scan surface |

⭐ **The sixth, verified on this tree before citing it, and the strongest one available: it is in `AGENTS.md` itself.** objectui#7800's defect was the 「怎么跑测试」 section asserting that the package-level test form reaches 「和 CI 同一个结论」. That was true when written — a claim about what objectui#3240 had just changed — and nothing re-derived it, so it went false while continuing to read as live. Its repair is already in `main` and in this branch's base; it narrows the claim to what measurement supports ("同一份配置不等于同一个结论") and adds the corrective writer-side rule. It is the file arguing about itself.

⭐ **And a seventh, which landed on `main` after the card was written** — objectui#9076, which is the commit this branch is cut from. Same shape: a gate header restated a ceiling and a baseline as literals, an authorised re-baseline moved the constants, the prose stayed, and for days nothing went red "because nothing fails on a number written in a comment". Its fix is this rule's prescribed shape, arrived at independently again: the header now names its subjects and renders neither, and the gate's verdict line prints the live reading on every run. The rule is describing something the repo is still paying for.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0. Printed: *"Compared the working tree with 3984bab5a (merge-base with origin/main): 1 file(s) changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 1 changeset(s) added."* then *"✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."* The changeset is present anyway, with **empty frontmatter** — this repo's explicit no-release declaration.
- `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`, `check-doc-links`, `check-doc-fence-languages`, `check-bash32-floor`, `check-governed-queue-guard --self-test`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major` — all exit 0, each read from its own verdict line rather than from a shell status.
- The six test files that read `AGENTS.md` as a corpus rather than mentioning it in a comment — the component-node vocabulary pin, the doc version-claims census, the site agent-files pin, and the doc-links, changeset-presence and governed-queue-guard suites — `6 passed (6)`, `230 passed (230)`.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test AGENTS.md` classifies this diff **GOVERNED**, one of one path, and states the terminal shape: park as a draft, human merge.

## ⛔ Governed surface — this PR stops at draft

`AGENTS.md` is the first row on this repo's governed-surface list. ⛔ Not flipped ready, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no auto-merge, ⛔ no approving review from this seat. A **human merge is the review record**. ⚠️ The `Governed Surface Queue Guard`'s `pull_request` leg exits 0 on purpose — a governed PR sitting in draft is its healthy terminal state, and green there is not a clearance to proceed.

The contract-review-tier review the ruling originally asked for was **lifted** on the card by the skills seat, on a maintainer ruling; the lane seat's default-tier review plus the gates is the review of record.
